elements.statement: The observed genre (dungeon roguelike) embeds narrative directly into its mechanical loops across all three exemplars: story functions as a retention lever, not a separate layer.
elements.ref: Cross-Game Architectural Synthesis > Reusable Architecture Bricks: 'Narrative/Lore Embedded in Mechanics: Stories unlock via boss defeats, escape counts, relationship flags. Story is not separate from grind; it rewards the grind.'

elements.statement: Absent a project charter, the only world-context defensible for a game in this lane is a genre-level frame: a self-contained dungeon or underworld space traversed across repeated attempts. This is a frame for downstream design, NOT a setting the project has chosen.
elements.ref: Per-game 'World & Setting' sections, three divergent settings with no convergent one: Hades 'set in the Greek Underworld'; Isaac 'procedurally generated basement dungeons'; Slay the Spire 'A mysterious Spire rises from a dark land'.

sections.reason: No project charter is present in the run (inputs_recus.charter=false; charter.yaml absent from the run_dir, state.json carries no charter reference). The worldscan records only the chronologies of three reference games (Zagreus's repeated escape attempts, Isaac's sequential boss ladder, the Spire's three acts). Those timelines belong to those games; importing any would fabricate a chronology this project has never defined.

The worldscan gives three DIVERGENT stakes: escape the Underworld (Hades), flee the mother's wrath (Isaac), ascend the Spire and defeat the Heart (Slay the Spire). Unlike the narrative-embedding pattern, no convergent genre stake exists to infer, and with charter absent nothing selects one. Grounding a single stake would mean inventing the project's central conflict.

No faction of this project's world is anchored anywhere. The worldscan names only entities of the reference games (the House of Hades NPCs; the four Slay the Spire ascendants Ironclad/Silent/Defect/Watcher), which belong to those worlds. With charter absent, no faction of amont_narratif_probe can be cited without invention.

The only protagonists and NPCs in the entries (Zagreus, Isaac, Ironclad/Silent/Defect/Watcher, Nyx, Meg, Persephone) are characters of the three reference games. This project has no defined protagonist or cast and charter is absent; any character posed here would be fabricated.

Character relations cannot be grounded when no character of this world is grounded (see 'characters'). The worldscan observes a reference game's relationship SYSTEM (Hades's NPC-bond / Nectar mechanic) as a reusable brick, but that is a mechanic of another game, not a relation within this project's world.

The worldscan's events (boss ladders, the death-and-return escape loop, act transitions) are events of the reference games. No event of this project's world is defined and charter is absent; grounding one would invent the world's history.

elements.statement: The worldscan observes a convergent narrative rule across all three exemplars: player failure is reframed as progress. Each failed run unlocks dialogue, relationship advancement, or lore.
elements.ref: Hades Retention Mechanics: 'Death is reframed as progress: every failure unlocks dialogue, relationship advancement, story beats.' Shared Retention Pattern: 'narrative/mechanical rewards for repeated failure.'

elements.statement: Coherence constraint inferred for any world built in this lane (pending a charter): the fiction must remain legible across repeated failure. A world whose story cannot survive the death-loop would contradict the genre's core retention lever.
elements.ref: Cross-Game synthesis 'narrative/mechanical rewards for repeated failure' + Hades loop: 'Upon escape, Zagreus withers on surface and is forced to return (narrative loop).'
